discovery: Discovery of transiting exoplanets and the opening of exoplanet atmospheric characterisation

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: In 1999 Charbonneau and Henry independently observed the transit of HD 209458b, the first planet seen passing in front of its star. This proved that radial-velocity signals came from real planets and gave the first radii and densities of planets outside the Solar System. In 2002 Charbonneau and colleagues detected sodium in that planet's atmosphere, which turned transits into a tool for spectroscopy. Seager's theoretical work on transmission spectra laid the physical foundation for that measurement, and her work on atmospheres and biosignatures defined how we now look for habitable worlds. Together they changed exoplanets from points on a velocity curve into physical objects with sizes, compositions and climates. Kepler, TESS, CHEOPS and JWST build directly on their work. It is the essential step from finding planets to asking whether life can exist on them.
